biggest_catch: TextMaster's official translator pages no longer exist — the entire site now redirects to the Acolad/Lia merge notice, and no translator pay rate, signup terms, or payment details are published anywhere on official pages, so earnings are completely unverifiable.
catches: No official published translator pay rate — the old translator FAQ that documented payment rules has been removed (URLs now redirect to the Acolad merge page).
TextMaster has joined Acolad and the platform is now 'Lia' — translator onboarding terms on official pages are effectively gone; whether new translators can even sign up is unclear.
Zero guaranteed tasks: crowdsourced platforms like this assign work per project with no income floor.
Qualification tests historically gated access (per third-party sources); current official pages say nothing.
An official PEMT FAQ snippet notes repetitions are not paid and TM 100% matches are only partially paid — but without rate figures this means effective pay can be pushed down on TM-heavy jobs.
Effective hourly pay can be low and variable; no official minimum or floor is published.

c1.evidence: TextMaster is a real company (crowdsourced translation/copywriting platform, raised €1.64M per TechCrunch 2012); official site confirms 'TextMaster has joined Acolad' with the Lia platform.

c2.evidence: FAIL — no official page publishes a translator pay rate or payment mechanism. textmaster.com/translator/ and /translator-writer/faq/ now both serve the Acolad merge notice; the only payment-related official FAQ found (PEMT repetition pay) states payment rules without any rate figure.

c3.evidence: No upfront fee is stated anywhere; historically translator registration was free.

c4.evidence: FAIL — no official statement of payout timing, method, or minimums for translators exists on current official pages.

eligibility: Cannot be confirmed from official pages: the translator signup and qualification terms have been removed in the Acolad transition. Historically TextMaster required a qualification test and vetted native-speaking translators; this is now legacy information, not official current terms.
notes: Read textmaster.com/translator/ and textmaster.com/translator-writer/faq/ (live 2026-09-23): both pages now display only the Acolad merge notice ('Meet Lia, the platform for all your translation needs'); translator recruitment, rates, and FAQ content are gone. Found one surviving official FAQ article via search (PEMT repetition pay: repetitions unpaid, TM 100% matches partially paid, all words paid in non-TM projects) — confirms payment is per-word but gives NO rate figure. Third-party sources cite €0.06/word-style figures but are NOT official and were excluded. Verdict 'reject': no official published pay figure or mechanism exists on current official pages. Could NOT confirm: any translator rate, payout method/timing/minimums, whether new translator signup is still open, or the 'Conditions' terms URL.

s1.note: No fee stated. Current eligibility/signup terms are not published on official pages after the Acolad merge.

s2.note: No official rate; per-word payment confirmed by an official FAQ snippet but with no figure — TM-heavy jobs pay less per the repetition rules; effective hourly pay can be low.

s4.note: No earnings claims on official pages to evaluate; the merge notice makes no income promises.
